title: pending_pause_overflow cleared on panic-unwind silently drops queued ERROR
evidence: On panic during a pause/resume cycle, the pending_pause_overflow queue is cleared without flushing — silent drop instead of structured ERROR synthesis.
recommendation: Drain the queue into ERROR cascades before clearing, or guard with RAII so the unwind path delivers the diagnostic.

title: Core::up(INVALIDATE) cascades via dep-walk instead of plain-forward
evidence: R1.4.2 specifies plain-forward semantics for INVALIDATE; current impl runs the cascade through dep-walk in Core::invalidate. Behavioral effect is identical for canonical scenarios but the implementation diverges from spec.
recommendation: Either lift the impl to plain-forward, or amend canonical-spec to bless dep-walk semantics. Track until alignment is decided.

title: Phase 3 of Core::register walks deps twice
evidence: Validation walks deps once in Phase 1 (lock-released) and again in Phase 3 (re-validation under state-lock). Caching the validated NodeId vector between phases removes one O(N) walk and a HashMap::get per dep.
recommendation: Cache validated NodeIds in a phase-1 scratch buffer; re-use in phase 3.

title: reset_for_fresh_lifecycle calls make_op_scratch lock-held
evidence: Lock-discipline asymmetry: make_op_scratch is lock-released in Core::register but lock-held inside reset_for_fresh_lifecycle. Inconsistent lock discipline across the same helper.
recommendation: Lift make_op_scratch out of the lock-held region in reset_for_fresh_lifecycle to match Core::register.

title: Asymmetric UnknownNode typed-error surface across Graph wrapper
evidence: Graph::derived returns Result<NodeId, NameError> for namespace conflicts; underlying Core call returns RegisterError. The wrapper layer doesn't surface RegisterError::UnknownDep distinctly. Callers can't differentiate name-conflict vs unknown-dep.
recommendation: Unify the wrapper error surface so RegisterError variants flow through with their semantic identity preserved.

title: Schedule Slice E2 — fn ctx + cleanup hooks
evidence: D054/D055 design locked 2026-05-07 for ctx + cleanup hooks per R2.4.5/R2.4.6. Implementation deferred. Open design questions: (a) ctx extends/replaces FnCtx, (b) binding-side storage shape.
recommendation: Lift Slice E2 once the two design questions resolve.

title: Eight parity scenarios unwritten — pending napi-rs binding
evidence: Behavioral traces 1–8 in report 005 (pause overflow, PausableMode consolidation, R1.3.2.d coalescing, replay buffer, Core::up, RegisterError, SetPausableModeError, OperatorFactoryError) have no parity coverage; rustImpl arm is dormant pending the binding.
recommendation: Author the eight scenarios when the napi-rs operator binding lands; activates the rustImpl arm.

title: Schedule TS port-back of PausableMode consolidation
evidence: Rust port adopted PausableMode { Default, ResumeAll, Off } as the canonical §2.6 model. TS still ships ResumeAll as default. Port-back scheduled in Phase 13.6.B migration scope.
recommendation: Land PausableMode rename + Default-as-canonical change in TS; keep behavior gated on opt-in flag during migration.

title: node.rs is 4.6K LOC — architectural splitting candidate
evidence: node.rs holds 43 pub fns + 18 pub struct/enum + 1 unsafe block. Citing 69 distinct spec rules across the file. By far the largest module in the workspace; concentration of dispatcher + lifecycle + register + pause logic. Cognitive load scales non-linearly past ~3K LOC.
recommendation: Investigate splitting along orthogonal concerns: dispatcher.rs (Core::up/emit/resolve), register.rs (Core::register), pause.rs (Core::pause/resume), terminal.rs (Core::complete/cleanup). Quantify with cargo-modules + per-fn LOC.

title: Only 25 of 222 spec rules have a doc-comment citation
evidence: Rule citation density: items.jsonl shows 25 distinct rule IDs cited across all crate doc comments. The canonical spec defines 222 rule IDs. Gap of ~89% — many rules implemented without an explicit code-side breadcrumb.
recommendation: Decide whether to (a) require rule-comment density at PR review time or (b) accept that high-traffic rules carry citations and the rest live in tests. Either way, surface the gap so it's a deliberate choice.
